propositions: Cloud transport has four distinct 429 behaviours across transport seam and dispatch level (ACLI subprocess with backoff, pooled REST without retry, bare urllib without retry, dispatch-wrapped with retry), none enumerated per-member and each must be asserted at its own boundary to avoid blind coverage.
Cloud lacks config-validation tests for non-HTTPS rejection, missing-credential loudness, and resolved-status configurability that DC gained, creating asymmetric hardening between adapters.

Every mutating Cloud transport member must be classified on two axes (transport seam × dispatch level) with duplicate-write safety assessment per known deliberate retry, recorded as a repo artifact table with completeness proven against git-grep enumeration and DC cross-check.

Cloud's probe.py hardcodes RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES as a per-deployment constant with no runtime override, while DC threads it from config; the decision of whether Cloud deployments with non-standard resolved-status names need a config hook (parity) or the constant suffices must be recorded at the definition site.

DC has no user-search method aliases so _bootstrap_account_id_via_user_search degrades to string matching; this degradation is unasserted and unprotected against accidental rename, requiring a pin test on the DC side.

Mutation-count assertions must be concrete per seam (urllib attempt count for REST, Popen call count for subprocess, bounded retry with Retry-After for dispatch wrapper) and mutation-checked by applying named perturbations (make one seam retry, suppress another's retry, add scheme check, remove backoff guard) to prove each sweep is not blind to its instrumentation boundary.
